feedback.problem:
$$
(\,∀x\in N,\,x>{n}_{\begin{aligned} \\ ↑ \\ \text{I}\end{aligned}}+1\,)⇒(\,∃z\in R,\,{{z}^{3}}_{\begin{aligned} \\ ↑ \\ \text{II}\end{aligned}}-1={y}_{\begin{aligned} \\ ↑ \\ \text{III}\end{aligned}}\,)
$$

Which occurrences of the variables in the expression above are free?
feedback.worked_solution:
Let's examine our expression and mark the occurrences of the variables as bound $(\text{b})$ or free $(\text{f}).$

- Occurrence I of the variable $n$ is *free* since it isn't placed right next to a quantifier and it doesn't lie within the scope of a quantifier that uses $n.$

- Occurrence II of the variable $z$ is *bound* since it lies within the scope of the quantifier $∃z$ that uses $z:$ 

$$
(\,∀x\in N,\,x>n+1\,)⇒(\,∃z\in R,\,\overset{\text{scope of }∃z}{\overset{⏞}{{z}^{3}-1={y}_{\begin{aligned} \\ ↑ \\ \text{b}\end{aligned}}}}\,)
$$

- Occurrence III of the variable $y$ is *free* since it isn't placed right next to a quantifier and it doesn't lie within the scope of a quantifier that uses $y.$

The occurrences of variables in the expression are as follows:

$$
(\,∀{x}_{\begin{aligned} \\ ↑ \\ \text{b}\end{aligned}}\in N,\,{x}_{\begin{aligned} \\ ↑ \\ \text{b}\end{aligned}}>{n}_{\begin{aligned} \\ ↑ \\ \text{f}\end{aligned}}+1\,)⇒(\,∃{z}_{\begin{aligned} \\ ↑ \\ \text{b}\end{aligned}}\in R,\,{{z}^{3}}_{\begin{aligned} \\ ↑ \\ \text{b}\end{aligned}}-1={y}_{\begin{aligned} \\ ↑ \\ \text{f}\end{aligned}}\,)
$$

Therefore, the free occurrence is "I and III only."
